passage:
The bus stop was a long walk from Jasleen's room above the seed shop, and the scooter search had dragged on for a month. Every evening brought another listing, another friend of a friend with a bike to sell.
On Friday night, tired of it, Jasleen took a notebook and wrote: three scooters, decide by Sunday. Saturday morning meant visits to two of them, and the third was one that Karthik at the corner garage had already looked over. For each, Jasleen wrote the price, the sound of the engine and the distance to the shop.
On Sunday evening Jasleen tapped the notebook, picked the one with the quieter engine, and paid a small advance. On Monday, Jasleen rode to work.

qa.a: Jasleen lives in a room above the seed shop.

qa.q: Why did Jasleen feel ready to stop searching on Friday night?
qa.a: Jasleen was tired of the month-long search and wanted an end to it, which is why the notebook limit of three scooters and a Sunday deadline was written.

qa.q: What other approach could Jasleen have used to choose among the three scooters?
qa.a: Jasleen could have asked Karthik at the corner garage to rank them, since a mechanic's judgement can settle a close call.

qa.q: How might Karthik see Jasleen's plan?
qa.a: Karthik had already looked over one scooter, so may see the plan as a clear task that makes helping easier than an open-ended search.

grounding: A young professional limits the search to three options and a Sunday deadline, turning an open hunt into a finite task.

passage: Siddiq had moved to Madrid for work and wanted to learn Spanish properly. For a month he'd looked at language schools: evening classes, weekend classes, online tutors, conversation clubs. Twenty-three bookmarks. Every Sunday he said, "Next week I'll decide." At lunch on Monday, his colleague Javier asked how the classes were going. Siddiq admitted he hadn't started. That evening he made a rule. He picked three schools near his flat or office, no more. He wrote on a sticky note: "Choose by Sunday. Good enough is good enough." He visited two on Wednesday and called the third on Thursday. On Saturday he signed up for Tuesday and Thursday evenings at the school ten minutes from the office. On Monday he told Javier, "Hola. Classes start tomorrow."

qa.q: How many bookmarks had Siddiq saved?
How did Siddiq feel when he admitted he hadn't started?
qa.a: He probably felt embarrassed, since every Sunday he'd said he would decide the next week.

qa.q: What made Siddiq's new method work?
qa.a: Limiting himself to three options and a Sunday deadline turned an endless search into a small task with an end.

qa.q: How might Javier see Siddiq's news on Monday?
qa.a: Javier would likely be amused and pleased that Siddiq finally started, and might offer to practise Spanish with him.

grounding: A young professional limits the search to three options with a Sunday deadline, turning an open search into a task with an end.

passage: At the school where Binita worked in administration, the staff canteen contract was ending, and she had been asked to pick a new caterer. For two weeks she'd collected menus, prices and reviews from nine caterers and felt more stuck each day. Her colleague Samir found her in the office on Tuesday with papers all over the table. "Pick three," he said. "Any three that meet the basics. Decide by Sunday." Binita frowned, then nodded. She crossed out six that were too far away or too expensive. On Thursday the three remaining sent sample lunches, and the teachers tasted them in the staffroom. By Friday afternoon she had chosen the one the teachers liked most. She put the other menus in a drawer and felt the tightness in her shoulders go.

qa.q: How many caterers had Binita collected information from?
What does the tightness leaving Binita's shoulders suggest?
qa.a: It suggests she felt relieved once the endless search turned into a decision.

qa.q: What could Binita do if the new caterer doesn't work out?
qa.a: Go back to the other two shortlisted menus in the drawer, rather than restarting with all nine.

qa.q: How might the teachers see the tasting on Thursday?
qa.a: The teachers would likely enjoy being asked and feel their opinions counted in the choice.

grounding: A young professional limits the options to three and decides by a set day, turning an open search into a task with an end.
